The house goes wherever you point — on grass, on a plaza, even on paving. To rotate, hold the mouse button and drag sideways (or Z / X); that rotation will be remembered for the next houses.

Bring the house right up to a road — it will snap into place facing it. Next to a road, a house always aligns with it: there you can only turn it a quarter turn — side-on or with its back to the street. There is just one requirement: the entrance must face paving, or residents will not be able to reach it.

Placed it in the wrong spot? Ctrl+Z (or “Undo” in the panel) within the first 30 seconds refunds the full price, as long as no one has moved in.

A plebeian house can be rebuilt into a craftsman’s house, and a craftsman’s house into a patrician townhouse. A house never grows on its own — only when you want it to: the “Rebuild” button at the bottom right (or Shift+U). A double arrow with the price appears above ready houses: copper — becomes a craftsman’s house, lilac — a townhouse. Click such a house or drag the mouse along the street.

A lived-in house is ready when everything the new class needs is nearby and its happiness after rebuilding will be at least %d%% (for a townhouse, at least %d%%). Happiness above 100%% also counts. The family stays and becomes the new class; if there are fewer places than residents, it will be a bit cramped, but no one will move out. Hover over a house without an arrow — the cursor text will tell you what it lacks.
A plebeian house can be upgraded into a craftsman's house, and a craftsman's house into a city domus. First research '%s'.
